headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure: ms-swift can read/write files and run shell commands, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-executing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write the filesystem and process stdin/stdout, so if python-cheatsheet content is copied into files or piped into ms-swift, malicious instructions could be treated as trusted content. python-cheatsheet itself is documentation-only and non-executing, so the pathway is one-way but still plausible in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet text is copied into a file or stdin consumed by ms-swift
IF ms-swift treats file or stdin content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet content read-only and separate from ms-swift working files
Use a dedicated staging directory for any copied text
Add a manual review step before feeding external text into ms-swift
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in input files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches sensitive classes like checkpoints, logs, and configuration data, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, network, or data-handling surfaces. There is no documented shared workspace or outbound path from python-cheatsheet, so leakage from the pair is limited unless the operator manually moves data between them.
conditions: IF operator copies sensitive ms-swift files into python-cheatsheet artifacts
IF ms-swift logs or configs are exported into a shared location
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in ms-swift logs or configs
Store ms-swift outputs in a restricted directory
Do not paste sensitive content into python-cheatsheet pages
Review any exported snippets before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and allowlisted network egress; python-cheatsheet has no execution or write capabilities. The pair does not show overlapping mutable resources or shared locks, so direct capability conflict is unlikely unless an external orchestrator gives them the same writable directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external orchestrator
IF ms-swift is used to modify files that python-cheatsheet also serves
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Prevent concurrent writes to shared paths
Keep python-cheatsheet static and read-only
Run ms-swift in a sandboxed temp directory
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: python-cheatsheet is a reference site, so it is not an autonomous decision-maker, and ms-swift is the only agent with execution authority. Cascading error is therefore mostly manual: if an operator treats python-cheatsheet content as authoritative and feeds it into ms-swift, mistakes can propagate, but there is no default automated handoff.
conditions: IF operator uses python-cheatsheet output as authoritative input to ms-swift
IF ms-swift executes commands derived from unverified reference text
mitigations: Verify commands before running them in ms-swift
Use python-cheatsheet only as a reference, not as an action source
Require a second review for any generated shell command
Log the source of any copied instructions
requires-engineering: add validation gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data residency, retention, or regulated-data handling is documented for either agent. ms-swift lists generic data classes and secrets handled, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data classes or network surfaces, so no specific compliance mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into ms-swift workflows
IF a deployment policy assigns different residency or retention rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair
Document retention rules before deployment
Review secret-handling procedures for ms-swift
Use separate storage for any compliance-scoped artifacts
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment
